resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Zoning Official, Borough of Cape May Point
requirements: Interior inspection of the structure or unit by the Zoning Official before settlement (key or lock box code needed)

fees.label: Certificate of Compliance inspection, per unit (capped at $300 per building)
fees.quote: Enclosed is the $100.00 fee/unit (not to exceed $300 per building) for this inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Compliance Application (name, mailing address, unit, street address, block, lot, date of settlement, and a key or lock box code for the interior inspection) and send it with the $100.00 per unit fee to the Office of the Zoning Official, Borough of Cape May Point, PO Box 490, Cape May Point, NJ 08212 (215 Lighthouse Avenue). Office hours are 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM Tuesday and Wednesday only.

evidence.quote: Please Inspect the following structure or unit:
Bruce Britton Zoning Official 609-884-8468 x16 bbritton@capemaypoint.org

resale_co.notes: The Borough's Certificate of Compliance Application (dated January 2025) asks the Zoning Official to inspect a structure or unit, asks for the date of settlement and a key or lock box code, and charges $100.00 per unit (not over $300 per building). It is listed under 'Zoning and Construction Applications' in the Borough Document Center, and the Zoning page says the Zoning Official issues all Certificates of Compliance. The form is plainly built for sales, but the ordinance text itself (ecode360 CA0524) could not be read, so the exact legal requirement, lead time and what is checked are not confirmed. The Borough's construction code work is done by the City of Cape May Construction Office under a shared services contract (Construction Official Lou Vito, 609-884-9555 x7). Cape May Point requires annual rental fire inspections before a rental permit is issued (Code Enforcement / Rental Inspector Brady Schoenrock, 609-884-8468 x21); that is a rental program, not a resale requirement. The Borough website blocks rapid automated requests, so pages were fetched slowly.

requirements: The State application certifies smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and the secondary power source identification label (homes with solar, generators or battery systems); it no longer lists a fire extinguisher

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (State is the fire code enforcing agency and issues smoke certificates)
authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days before closing for the lowest fee

fees.label: More than 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: If you are applying for a certificate more than ten business days from the closing date the fee is $45 dollars

fees.label: 4 to 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: if applying 4 to 10 business days from the closing date the fee is $90

fees.label: Less than 4 business days before closing
fees.quote: if the closing date is less than four business days the fee is $161.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'). Payment by e-check or credit card is required before submitting, and a valid email address is required. Homes heated by electricity with no CO alarm requirement should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.
authorities.contact_title: Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (listed as Fire Official in the state fire directory)

evidence.quote: LEAID: 0503-999 Enf Auth. State Fire Official Louis Kilmer Phone (609)633-6132

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Cape May Point as 'S' (the State enforces the fire code) and DCA's July 17, 2026 list of state-enforced towns marks it 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates). The DCA Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement page lists Louis Kilmer with phone (609) 633-6106; the state fire directory lists (609) 633-6132. The volunteer Cape May Point Fire Company is not the enforcing agency.
